messages:
Laura: heads-up — saw a kv-cache miss spike (~3x) on the FP8-optimized model when continuous-batching hit an AWQ fallback path overnight. metric spike at ~00:12 UTC, looks correlated with a sudden surge of short seq requests.
Diego: ugh. did the routing fall back to the AWQ variant because of capacity or a kernel crash?
Laura: fallback reason reported: "quant_variant_mismatch". Infra bot posted the rollout and a small autoscale event right before the spike.
infra-bot: DeployRollbackDetector: rollback_attempt=0, fallback_policy=hybrid-quant-fallback, region=us-west2, event_ts=00:10
Chen: can you paste the snippet from the kvcache logs? curious about prefix keys and TTLs.
Laura: pasted below — looks like kvcache evictions + hits go down, then continuous-batcher queues increase.
```
[00:11:58] kvcache: prefix='user:ctx:v2' hit=false ttl=0 eviction=true
[00:11:59] batcher: enqueue id=0x7f32 seq_len=8 model=fp8-xxl batcher_size=1
[00:12:00] route: switched_to=awq-compat model_variant=awq-int8 reason=quant_variant_mismatch
[00:12:01] kvcache: prefix='user:ctx:v2' hit=false ttl=0 eviction=true
[00:12:02] batcher: enqueue id=0x7f33 seq_len=16 model=fp8-xxl batcher_size=2
[00:12:05] kvcache: miss_rate=0.62 sampling_window=60s
[00:12:07] swap: kv-coalescer dropped=3
```
Sasha: hmm short seqs cause more prefix churn; AWQ variant has different kv key layout so cache lookup misses after fallback. mixing quant formats may be the issue.
Matt: also FP8 runtime keeps dense-prefetch warmup that AWQ doesn't honor, so when we fallback we lose the warmed KV entries. that would explain the increased token latency too.
Diego: we should avoid flipping to AWQ mid-request routing unless cache compatibility is guaranteed. suggestion: add a compatibility-bit to route decision or require cache flush/sync.
Laura: another quick data point: running shadow test with same traffic but pinned to AWQ did not show the churn; it's the cross-variant handoff that kills cache locality.
Chen: propose immediate mitigation: set fallback_policy=reject_or_queue for hybrid-quant for 24h on the affected pool, and lower continuous-batcher.max_latency to reduce cross-batch churn. thoughts?
Sasha: +1 on reject_or_queue for now. we should also add a metric that tags kvcache hits by model_variant_pair (from->to) so we can observe handoffs.
Matt: quick config snippet to try:
```
routing.hybrid_quant.fallback = "queue"
routing.hybrid_quant.compatibility_check = true
batcher.continuous.max_latency_ms = 8
kvcache.prefetch.ttl_ms = 120000
```
Diego: agree. can we run a 1h canary with queue fallback on a small percentage (5%) first, then flip 100%? also add alert if kv miss_rate > 0.3 for 5m.
Laura: I'll schedule the canary and add the kvcache-pairing metric. assigning: Laura -> run canary + dashboard, Chen -> implement metric + alert, Diego -> prepare rollback playbook, Matt -> validate prefetch TTL interplay in local sim.
Chen: I’ll add a short eval harness to replay the short-seq distribution so we can run regression tests before the next rollout.
Sasha: good. capture on-call notes in the incident channel if anything escalates. thanks all :thumbsup:
Diego: one follow-up: we should document kv key schema per quant variant in onboarding docs so model owners know compatibility constraints. ticket inbound.
Laura: filing ticket now: infra/quant-kv-compat (includes reproducer + logs).
infra-bot: TicketCreated: infra/quant-kv-compat #3421 assigned=diego, priority=high
Laura: closing loop here — will post canary results in ~1.5h.
